overrides.hook: We deleted the sentence we wanted buyers to remember most.
progression: Confess the strongest unsupported homepage sentence before explaining the product.
Show the four empty witness boxes that forced its removal.
Turn the deletion into a repeatable founder-side claim audit.
Invite a before-and-after decision without promising a public verdict.
body: OPERATING TENSION: Our draft said, ‘An AI GTM employee that makes any brand go viral.’ It was memorable. It also had no independent preference win, observed organic breakout, attributed conversion, or proven revenue behind it.
DECISION RULE: After every outcome sentence, add ‘according to what?’ If the answer is a model output, internal opinion, or future plan, move the sentence to HYPOTHESIS or delete it.
PROOF BOUNDARY: The approved evidence is narrower than the deleted outcome, stays attached to its source, and preserves human release control. Market response remains unobserved.
PRACTITIONER ACTION: Open your homepage, find the sentence you would least want a skeptical buyer to cross-examine, and create a before-and-after version with that line removed.
FAILS WHEN: The deletion exposes no decision-relevant gap, changes no buyer interpretation, or merely replaces one unsupported superlative with another.
overrides.cta: Delete one line, then inspect the evidence before deciding whether to join the design-partner review.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Mark one homepage sentence FACT, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS, or BLOCKED, then keep the before-and-after version private unless a named owner approves sharing.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when qualified operators cannot identify a changed release or buying decision after deleting one unsupported sentence.

overrides.hook: POV: your best homepage line just got asked for one witness.
progression: Open on a cursor hovering over the most seductive sentence.
Make four empty evidence boxes appear before any narration explains them.
Delete the sentence in one irreversible-looking visual beat.
End with a pauseable test the viewer can run immediately.
body: 0:00 VISUAL: Owned browser capture — highlight ‘makes any brand go viral’; four boxes slam in: INDEPENDENT WIN, ORGANIC BREAKOUT, ATTRIBUTED CONVERSION, PROVEN REVENUE. All read NO WITNESS.
0:02 VO: This was our favorite line. Then we asked it for one witness.
0:06 PROOF: The cursor deletes the sentence. A smaller source-bound product statement remains beside an exact evidence reference. On-screen tag: MARKET RESPONSE NOT OBSERVED.
0:12 ACTION: Pause. Open your homepage. Which sentence disappears when you add ‘according to what?’
overrides.cta: Run the witness check on one line; inspect the product only if the deletion changes your decision.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Pause on the four witness boxes, test one public sentence locally, and save a private before-and-after screenshot for the release owner.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when viewers cannot repeat the test, identify the unsupported line, or understand why the narrower replacement is different.

overrides.hook: We deleted our best launch headline because the model could not produce a single witness for it.
progression: Disclose builder affiliation and publish the embarrassing sentence first.
Describe the exact evidence request that the sentence failed.
Show the narrower replacement and the commercial trade-off honestly.
Invite counterexamples instead of harvesting generic launch praise.
body: AFFILIATION: We built ProofLaunch Cortex-X. This is a build-in-public teardown of our own copy, not an independent recommendation.

WHAT FAILED: The line was ‘An AI GTM employee that makes any brand go viral.’ We asked for an independent preference win, an observed breakout, an attributed conversion, or proven revenue. The record contained none.
MECHANISM: We deleted the line and kept only the approved bounded product fact beside its evidence reference. The desired market outcome stays a hypothesis until an authorized observation exists.

TRADE-OFF: The replacement is less exciting and may earn less attention. It is also the only version we can defend today. The useful question is whether that constraint creates better decisions or merely safer prose.
overrides.cta: Stress-test the rule with a counterexample; inspect the design-partner material only if the trade-off matters to your team.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Audit one redacted claim pattern or counterexample—never confidential copy—and identify which witness should be sufficient to keep the line.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when practitioners show a common, defensible outcome sentence that the witness rule wrongly rejects or cannot classify.

overrides.hook: I put forty AI GTM claims on trial. Thirty-nine should not reach a homepage.
progression: Cold-open with forty face-down claim cards and one visible verdict slot.
Reveal the most seductive rejected sentence before introducing the test.
Apply the same four-witness rule across contrasting claim types.
Give buyers a rejection test before mentioning the product cohort.
body: TITLE: I Put 40 AI GTM Claims on Trial — 39 Should Not Reach a Homepage
THUMBNAIL: Forty black cards, thirty-nine stamped NO WITNESS, one white card left standing. Text: WHICH ONE SURVIVED?

0:00-0:30: ‘Makes any brand go viral.’ It sounds like a winning headline. The record contains no independent win, breakout, attributed conversion, or proven revenue. We delete it on camera, then test the remaining thirty-nine claims by the same rule.
CHAPTER: The Sentence We Wanted; Four Acceptable Witnesses; Aspirations Disguised as Results; The One Bounded Claim; Run the Test on Your Vendor; What Evidence Could Reverse a Rejection.
RECOMMENDATION BOUNDARY: This is a synthetic buyer-audit film using our own materials. It demonstrates the test, not customer preference, market lift, conversion, revenue, or superiority.
overrides.cta: Use the four-witness chapter on one vendor demo before opening the ProofLaunch evidence pack.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Choose the surviving claim before the reveal, record the witness you relied on, then compare that rule with the film’s bounded verdict.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when qualified buyers cannot apply the witness rule to another vendor or cannot explain what evidence would reverse a rejection.

overrides.hook: The most honest redesign on your homepage may be one black rectangle.
progression: Use a redaction block as the recognisable visual object.
Reveal why the missing sentence failed without turning slides into legal copy.
Replace the deleted promise with one bounded product fact.
Make the final slide a saveable four-witness audit card.
body: SLIDE 1: Screenshot-style homepage. One giant line is blacked out. Caption on image: WE DELETED THE SENTENCE WE WANTED MOST.
SLIDE 2: Under the redaction: ‘makes any brand go viral.’ Four empty witness boxes sit beneath it: WIN, BREAKOUT, CONVERSION, REVENUE.
SLIDE 3: Verdict card: NO WITNESS. Not false forever. Unsupported today. Move it to hypothesis or remove it from public proof.
SLIDE 4: What remains: the approved source-bound product fact beside its evidence reference. Small footer: market response not observed.
SLIDE 5: SAVE THIS TEST — after any outcome claim, ask ‘according to what?’ Circle FACT, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS, or BLOCKED.
overrides.cta: Save the witness card and delete one unsupported line before inspecting the cohort.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Create a private redacted screenshot of one claim, label its evidence state, and share it only with explicit owner approval.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when the redaction is read as a gimmick, the four states remain unclear, or the exercise changes no release decision.

overrides.hook: Three words expose the difference between a marketing claim and its evidence: according to what.
progression: State a repeatable three-word category test in the first post.
Apply it to the strongest rejected claim without hedging.
Publish the strongest objection to the test before the verdict.
End with the evidence condition that would change the decision.
body: 1/ Read your homepage aloud. After every outcome claim, add the words ‘according to what.’ A model draft, internal opinion, or future plan leaves a hypothesis wearing a result’s clothes.
2/ Ours said ‘makes any brand go viral.’ The answer was no independent win, no observed breakout, no attributed conversion, and no proven revenue. We deleted it.
3/ Strongest objection: early products need ambitious language before they have outcome data. Agreed. Ambition belongs in the mission or hypothesis—not inside a sentence presented as observed proof.
4/ The line can return when a named population, period, source, and limitation support it. Until then, the narrower product fact is the only public witness.
overrides.cta: Add ‘according to what?’ to one sentence; inspect ProofLaunch only if the answer changes the claim.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Label one non-private claim pattern with its evidence class and the witness that would legitimately change it.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when informed readers cannot distinguish ambition from asserted evidence or the test rejects clearly bounded opinion and prediction.

overrides.hook: To audit an AI marketing claim, identify the population, period, source, and limitation before judging the wording.
progression: Answer the substantiation query with a four-field test immediately.
Apply the test to one disclosed synthetic claim and bounded replacement.
Name when the method is inappropriate or incomplete.
Let the searcher finish the audit without signup or sales context.
body: DIRECT ANSWER: For each outcome claim, record four fields: who or what was observed, during which period, from which authorized source, and with which limitation. Missing fields keep the statement in hypothesis, not proof.

DECISION CRITERIA: A claim may proceed to human review when its factual clauses resolve to authorized evidence and its inference, uncertainty, owner, and release state remain explicit. A desired result without an observation is rejected from public proof.
WHEN NOT TO USE: This editorial test is not legal advice, scientific validation, or a substitute for specialist review in regulated, comparative, financial, medical, or safety-sensitive claims.

EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: In this owned synthetic example, ‘makes any brand go viral’ has no independent win, observed breakout, attributed conversion, or proven revenue; the method demonstrates classification only.
NEXT STEP: Copy one homepage outcome sentence into four rows—population, period, source, limitation—and delete or relabel every clause whose row remains empty.
overrides.cta: Complete the four-field audit, then inspect the design-partner evidence before deciding whether to join.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Audit one public sentence locally and retain the four-field record with the named release owner; no submission is required.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when the four fields cannot distinguish an observed fact from opinion, prediction, mission, or clearly labeled hypothesis.

overrides.hook: A marketing claim is not simply true or false; its release state depends on evidence, inference, authority, and unresolved conditions.
progression: Resolve the category ambiguity with four stable evidence states.
Separate the people and objects that hold different kinds of authority.
Name the exception where a bold claim remains appropriate.
Route unresolved clauses to a concrete owner decision.
body: ENTITY MAP: Brief supplies intent; evidence object supplies authorized facts; editor supplies inference; reviewer supplies judgment; release owner supplies external-action authority; observation supplies later market evidence.

COMPARISON CRITERIA: FACT has an authorized source; INFERENCE is a disclosed interpretation; HYPOTHESIS is a testable future proposition; BLOCKED lacks the evidence, rights, permission, or specialist review needed for release.
EXCEPTION: Mission, opinion, prediction, and creative metaphor may remain bold when their form is unmistakable and the net impression does not convert them into factual outcomes.

SOURCE BOUNDARY: The ProofLaunch record supports preparation of review-ready assets from a rights-bound brief; it does not establish publication, audience response, conversion, revenue, or product superiority.
OWNER ACTION: Label each factual clause, attach its source or unresolved condition, and route only the remaining release decision to the accountable human.
overrides.cta: Map one claim into the four evidence states before considering a product review.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Label every clause in one public sentence and mark the first handoff where evidence or authority becomes ambiguous.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this map when common claim types cannot be classified without concealing a material exception or changing the sentence’s net impression.

overrides.hook: The fastest useful audit of an AI marketing claim asks what was observed, when, where the evidence lives, and what the claim leaves out.
progression: Give the direct method before introducing any product context.
Use a disclosed owned example to show rejection and repair.
Separate editorial classification from legal or scientific validation.
Publish the exact evidence status and update date.
body: QUESTION: How can a team audit an AI-generated marketing claim before publishing it?

DIRECT ANSWER: Break the claim into factual clauses, then record the population, period, authorized source, and limitation for each clause. Label every remainder FACT, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS, or BLOCKED.

METHOD: Compare the wording with its evidence object and net impression; preserve disclosed uncertainty; identify the human release owner; reject any outcome presented as observed when no qualifying observation exists.
LIMITATION: This is an editorial and operational audit, not legal advice or specialist substantiation. Regulated and comparative claims require the appropriate qualified review.
UPDATED: 2026-08-03 — the owned ProofLaunch example has preparation evidence but no observed market effect.
overrides.cta: Apply the four fields to one sentence before inspecting the design-partner evidence pack.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Audit one public claim without confidential material and record the single witness that would change its release state.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop citing this audit when it cannot preserve the difference between fact, opinion, prediction, metaphor, and explicitly labeled hypothesis.

overrides.campaign_platform: The Claim That Should Stay Bold
overrides.hook: Not every unsupported sentence should be deleted; some should be relabeled so ambition remains visible without impersonating evidence.
progression: Begin with the counterexample that breaks an overzealous fact-checking rule.
Separate mission, prediction, metaphor, and observed outcome by net impression.
Show how audience and placement alter the appropriate label.
End with a decision framework that can preserve boldness.
body: COMMON MODEL: If a marketing sentence lacks outcome evidence, delete it or replace it with a narrow factual description.

COUNTEREXAMPLE: ‘We want every small team to launch with evidence’ is an ambition, not an observed outcome. Deleting it removes strategic meaning; presenting it as achieved would mislead. The right repair is a visible mission or hypothesis label.
BOUNDARY CONDITIONS: Evaluate grammar, placement, surrounding proof, audience sophistication, comparison target, materiality, and the sentence’s overall impression—not keyword presence alone.

DECISION FRAMEWORK: Preserve bounded mission, opinion, prediction, and metaphor; source factual clauses; disclose inference; keep future outcomes in hypothesis; block claims whose evidence, rights, permission, or specialist review is missing.
UPDATED: 2026-08-03 — this framework has no production-effect observation.
overrides.cta: Use the counterexample before deleting a bold line; inspect ProofLaunch only if relabeling changes the decision.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Classify one sentence by communicative form and net impression, then choose keep, source, relabel, test, or block with a written reason.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this framework when qualified reviewers cannot agree on the communicative form or it conceals a materially misleading overall impression.

overrides.hook: A black rectangle can carry more trustworthy information than the polished sentence it replaces.
progression: Bind the deleted text, redaction image, and evidence state to one entity.
Use only producible owned media with no simulated customer response.
Make the visual change determine a concrete release decision.
Expose where cross-modal consistency still proves nothing about effect.
body: ENTITY: The owned ProofLaunch homepage draft is under evaluation; one outcome claim is removed, one bounded statement remains, and no market response is established.
TEXT EVIDENCE: Removed line—‘makes any brand go viral.’ The retained approved evidence remains source-bound, while market response remains unobserved.
MEDIA EVIDENCE: Produce an owned before-and-after homepage pair, four empty witness boxes, and a visible NO WITNESS redaction; include no customer, testimonial, social counter, or simulated result.
RELATIONSHIP: The redaction visually encodes the same evidence-state change described by the text, allowing the reviewer to confirm that the unsupported outcome no longer appears as public proof.
LIMITATION: Cross-modal consistency demonstrates representational discipline for this fixture only; it does not establish audience preference, organic breakout, conversion, revenue, or superiority.
overrides.cta: Compare the retained text with every frame, then inspect the evidence before deciding whether to join the cohort.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Inspect each frame for the deleted outcome, retained bounded fact, evidence state, and absence of implied customer response.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when any frame restores the deleted outcome, implies a customer result, or cannot be traced to the owned text record.

overrides.campaign_platform: What Can Be Claimed Before Launch
overrides.hook: Before launch, process evidence can support what a system produced and governed—not how a market responded.
progression: Frame a narrow research question with an explicit pre-launch cutoff.
Separate owned process records from every missing market source.
Name the disagreement that creates premature effect claims.
Translate the source gap into a conservative release decision.
body: RESEARCH QUESTION: Which claims about an AI GTM system are supportable before any authorized publication, audience response, conversion event, reconciled revenue, or independent product comparison exists?

SOURCE MAP: Owned records may establish the brief, source rights, generated artifact, review history, permission state, and human release decision. Independent preference, delivery, audience, conversion, and revenue sources are absent here.
FINDING: The current evidence supports only the approved bounded preparation fact. It does not support virality, conversion, revenue, agency-level preference, or superiority.
DISAGREEMENT: Teams often treat polished creative, model scores, or green regression tests as market evidence; those sources establish production behavior, not external response.
DECISION IMPLICATION: Release only the bounded preparation fact, keep desired outcomes in a preregistered hypothesis, and wait for the corresponding authorized observation before revising the claim.
UPDATED: 2026-08-03 — no production effect observed.
overrides.cta: Audit the source class behind one pre-launch claim before inspecting the product evidence pack.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Map available process evidence against missing market evidence, then identify the first claim that crosses the boundary.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this answer when a cited source actually observes the relevant population, period, outcome, and limitation and therefore supports a broader bounded claim.

overrides.hook: A claim review is incomplete until release can be denied and the exact rejected sentence remains preserved.
progression: Separate public evidence from tenant-authorized review context.
Present keep, relabel, test, and block as explicit decision options.
Bind the chosen action to a human owner and immutable sentence.
Hand off an auditable record without executing an external action.
body: PERMISSION BOUNDARY: This packet may read the exact authorized draft and evidence references; it grants no authority to publish, send, spend, enrich identities, or change strategy.

AUTHORIZED EVIDENCE: The approved product fact may enter beside its rights-bound brief, clause-level source, editorial inference, review history, and named human decision; unapproved tenant data may not.

DECISION OPTIONS: KEEP a sourced factual clause, RELABEL disclosed mission or hypothesis, TEST a preregistered future proposition, or BLOCK a clause missing evidence, rights, permission, or specialist review.
OWNER ACTION: The release owner selects one option for the exact sentence hash, records the unresolved condition, and separately authorizes any later external action.
AUDIT HANDOFF: Preserve the original line, revised line, evidence reference, decision reason, reviewer identity, timestamp, denied actions, and evidence required to reverse the decision.
overrides.cta: Run Delete Before Deploy on one sentence, then inspect the evidence before deciding whether to join the design-partner review.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Choose KEEP, RELABEL, TEST, or BLOCK for one exact sentence and record the evidence that could legitimately reverse that choice.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this packet when an authorized operator cannot deny release, reconstruct the decision, or distinguish public evidence from tenant context.
